question.problem: Consider the surface ${e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}=e-3.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,1,-1),$ what is the value of $\frac{a-b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)={e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=e-3.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2}))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}-2{z}^{2})k \\  & =(y{e}^{xy}-2x)i+(x{e}^{xy})j+(-4z)k \\ ∇f(1,1,-1) & =((1){e}^{(1)(1)}-2(1))\text{ }i+(1){e}^{(1)(1)}\text{ }j+(-4)(-1)\text{ }k \\  & =(e-2)\text{ }i+e\text{ }j+4\text{ }k \\  & =⟨e-2,\,e,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨e-2,\,e,\,4⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{a-b}{c}=\frac{(e-2)-e}{4}=-\frac{1}{2}.$
